🚨 Urgent — GOOG may already be through its $333.90 stop

The live feed is down (see outage note below), so this is not the deterministic price this report normally relies on — but two independent web snapshots put GOOG's Sept 9 close at $328.38 and $330.65, both below your $333.90 plain STOP, against a previous close cited at $338.36. The numbers don't agree with each other (exactly why search isn't used for prices normally), but they agree on direction: GOOG has likely traded through the stop. Headline context: "GOOGL stock slides as legal risks mount and AI battle heats up" (Sept 9) plus a delayed Alphabet-Blackstone data center project and EU search-remedy friction — real headwinds, not noise. Open IBKR now. If the stop triggered, confirm the fill price and update portfolio.json via portfolio-manager. If it didn't trigger despite price trading through $333.90, that's a broken protection you need to fix today — replace it immediately.

🚨 Urgent — SPXC halal-breach exit still not done (16 days overdue)

Third consecutive report flagging this (Sept 8, Sept 9, and now today). The Kranze defense-electronics compliance breach was logged 2026-08-25 — 16 days ago. The standing rule is exit at the next market open, regardless of P&L. portfolio.json still shows SPXC sitting on a passive $205 sell-limit with a $186.90 stop underneath — that is not the same thing as exiting. Cancel the resting $205 limit and exit at market (or an aggressive marketable limit) today, regardless of price. If it already filled and the record just hasn't synced, tell portfolio-manager so it catches up — but don't assume that; act on what's actually resting on the book.

⚠️ Price feed down — second day running

Yahoo Finance (query1 + query2) and the stooq fallback all returned network-egress-blocked errors from this environment again today — same failure as yesterday's report. No verified live price for GOOG or SPXC either day now. This looks like a persistent environment/network policy issue rather than a one-off — worth a look if it keeps happening. Trust IBKR directly, not this report, for anything price-dependent today.

📚 Today you learned

Execution Risk vs. Market Risk

Market risk is the thing you're used to from forex: price moves against you after you're in. Execution risk is different — it's the risk that the decision you already made correctly never actually gets carried out in the market. SPXC is the clean example right now: the call to exit on the defense-segment breach was right the day it was made, 16 days ago. The risk since then hasn't been "is this still the right call" — it's been "is a passive $205 limit order actually going to close this position," and the answer has been no, silently, for over two weeks. GOOG's stop question this morning is the same failure mode from a different angle: even a well-placed stop is only protection if it's confirmed to have fired. A good decision with broken execution behind it is functionally the same as no decision at all. The fix in both cases isn't more analysis — it's an active order and a confirmed fill, checked directly against the broker, not assumed from yesterday's plan.

Also today: Decision debt — every day a made-but-unexecuted decision sits open, it accrues risk on top of whatever the market is doing, independent of whether the original call was right.

Research output, not financial advice. Past performance does not guarantee future results. Verify halal compliance quarterly on Zoya or Musaffa.
